description: Synthetic, committed, network-free. Every case is answerable from the fixtures under sources/ and the transcripts under transcripts/. Cases select their own profile: the failing fixtures live in profiles of their own so a source that always fails cannot make every case report degraded coverage. Budgets and thresholds here are absolute first-run placeholders, to be replaced by regression bounds once measured distributions exist.

baseline.note: Measured over 41 cases on darwin/arm64, all nine gates passing. nDCG@10 0.7665, Recall@5 0.9028, Recall@20 1.0, MRR@10 0.6553, Success@5 1.0; abstention, coverage, provenance, source-outcome and locator accuracy all 1.0. Cold and warm runs produced identical metrics - the index is rebuilt at handshake either way, so there is no warm path to diverge from - and p95 was 81ms against a 400ms budget, roughly 5x headroom rather than a number tuned to just pass. exact_identifier_success_at_1 is 0.4 and is recorded as a floor, not a target: two of five identifier cases put a document's title chunk above the section judged authoritative, which is the first thing worth improving. Re-recorded 2026-07-27 for td-92c7b7, which stopped a question admitting a chunk that carries one of its terms and nothing else. Every required lineage in this pack is still returned and every gate still passes; pooled nDCG@10 rose 0.7668 to 0.7762 and MRR@10 0.6563 to 0.7089, and Recall@5 and Recall@20 are unchanged at 0.9444 and 1.0. What moved down is named rather than averaged away: nDCG in the alias, lineage and near-miss tag groups, and Recall@5 in the handbook and notes source families, because three cases lose a chunk judged 2 that was reached by a single word — runbooks/backup-restore.md#L3-L7 was retrieved for "what do we do after we lose data" on the word "we", and glossary.md#L3-L7 for a question about clustering on the word "record". Those are the retrievals this pack was measuring as successes and the ticket was written to stop; the result sets they came from went from ten and fifteen results to one and four. A pack that is a floor under retrieval quality has to record that trade rather than absorb it, which is what this paragraph is. Re-recorded 2026-07-28 for td-c5ef32, which lets a query term reach the other grammatical number of itself, but only where the source holds no spelling of that term at all. Every gate still passes and nothing measured moved down: pooled nDCG@10 rose 0.7856 to 0.7964 and every other pooled metric is unchanged, including MRR@10 at 0.7096 — the rule reorders nothing that was already found, because a term the corpus spells the caller's way is never expanded. The gain is one case reaching a chunk it had been missing on a plural. Re-recorded for td-54973d after replacing personal actor names in the synthetic signal fixtures; the queries and measured rankings are unchanged. Re-recorded 2026-07-29 for td-82176a, which adds the paraphrase-semantic family: five questions whose answer shares at most one content term with them, over a new household corpus under the notes source's own home directory, one of which must abstain because its answer is genuinely absent. Nothing about retrieval changed and nothing regressed: the per-case scores and returned lineage of all forty-one earlier cases are identical to the previous baseline, and the new fixtures share no content term with any earlier query, so no new chunk competes for an existing answer. What moved is the population. Pooled nDCG@10 0.7964 to 0.7236, Recall@5 0.9444 to 0.8500, Recall@20 1.0 to 0.9000, MRR@10 0.7096 to 0.6329, Success@5 1.0 to 0.9000; the paraphrase tag group nDCG@10 0.6696 to 0.3263 and Recall@5 1.0 to 0.4286, the document group 0.8032 to 0.6697, and the notes and handbook source families 0.7672 to 0.6771 and 0.8457 to 0.7853. Those decreases are the deliverable rather than a cost to justify: the gap that motivates semantic retrieval was previously unmeasurable in this pack, and a pack in which an unanswerable-by-words question does not lower anything is a pack that cannot see the problem. The new paraphrase-semantic group states it alone: nDCG@10 0.0689, Recall@5 0, Recall@20 0, MRR@10 0, Success@5 0 over four graded cases. Three score exactly zero; the fourth scores 0.2754 because what came back was a genuinely related neighbour graded 1 — the garden tip run instead of bin night. All four answer rather than abstain, which is the finding: a passage covering two ordinary words clears the admission floor while the passage that actually answers, covering one or none, never scores, so the lexical baseline is confidently wrong about the wrong machine, room or winter job instead of silent. Each of the four declares expected_top_lineage and marks it expected_fail, so the gap is a named defect the expected_failures_current gate will force somebody to unmark when a semantic source closes it, rather than a low number that becomes normal. The fifth case is deliberately ungraded: its abstention is correct, and an undefined ranking metric is not a zero. All eleven gates still pass, abstention accuracy is 1.0 over forty-six cases, exact_identifier_success_at_1 is unchanged at 0.4, and p95 was 62ms against the 400ms budget. This is the `documents` half of the head-to-head td-82176a exists to produce; a qmd source graded on these same judgments is what the numbers above are the baseline for.
